subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If 1, −2, 3 are the roots of x³ − 2x² + ax + 6 = 0, then find a.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find a — which root you substitute and what it gives.
insider_note: Substituting x = 1 is two lines; the pairwise-product relation a₂/a₀ = −5 is the check, and either route earns both marks.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute a root
steps.margin_note: First mark. A root makes the equation true, so put x = 1 in. Any of the three roots works; 1 gives the least arithmetic.
steps.memory_tip: A root makes the equation true, so put x = 1 in. Of the three, 1 gives the least arithmetic.
lines: 1 is a root, so x = 1 satisfies the equation:

recall.must_convey: That because 1 is a root, x = 1 is substituted into the equation.
accept: one is a root so put x equals one into the equation
substitute the root one and the equation must give zero
a root satisfies the equation so use x equals one
one root kabatti x equals one substitute cheyyali
put x equal to one because it is a root

steps.why: A root is a value that makes the polynomial 0, so substituting it gives an equation in the unknown coefficient a. This is faster than the root relations when only one coefficient is missing. (The relation a₂/a₀ = sum of pairwise products = (1)(−2) + (−2)(3) + (3)(1) = −5 gives the same a.)
common_mistakes: Substituting x = −2 or 3, which is correct but takes more arithmetic.

steps.label: Find a
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 1 − 2 + a + 6 = 0 gives a = −5. Check: the pairwise products of 1, −2, 3 add to −2 − 6 + 3 = −5 = a₂/a₀.
steps.memory_tip: 1 − 2 + a + 6 = 0 gives a = −5. Check: the pairwise products −2 − 6 + 3 = −5 = a₂/a₀.

accept: one minus two plus a plus six is zero so a is minus five
simplify and a plus five equals zero
one minus two plus a plus six zero, kabatti a minus five
a comes out as minus five

steps.why: The sum-of-pairwise-products relation is the free check: (1)(−2) + (−2)(3) + (3)(1) = −5 = a₂/a₀. Two routes agreeing is how a three-line answer proves itself.
common_mistakes: Writing a = 5 from a sign slip.
Not checking with a second root or with the pairwise-product relation.
